mainTopic: Honesty at the time of the חורבן; rescuing food and clothing from a fire on שבת; stopping a fire indirectly
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a discussion from the previous page. רבא had said ירושלים was destroyed because it had no אנשי אמנה (trustworthy people), and רב קטינא challenged him with a פסוק in ישעיה showing that people still admitted the truth about their Torah learning. The גמרא resolves this: people were honest about Torah, but not in business. A new משנה then allows saving a whole basket of loaves, a fig cake, or a barrel of wine from a fire on שבת, and discusses where the items may go and how many garments one may wear out. The גמרא reconciles this with the earlier three-meal limit, decides that filling one vessel counts as 'rescuing', and explains the helpers' 'calculation' after שבת. A ברייתא records רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי on wearing garments out of the fire, including רבי יוסי's list of eighteen garments. A final משנה allows blocking a fire with a goat hide or a wall of vessels, while רבי יוסי forbids new clay pots full of water. The גמרא quotes רב permitting water on the unburnt side of a garment and challenges him with a ברייתא; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading 'Be a chief over us' as a request for Torah leadership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues רב קטינא's proof from ישעיה. The people beg a man to lead them because he has Torah knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah matters that people cannot understand without first getting them wrong are in your hands, so 'be a chief over us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining רב קטינא's פסוק. People ask someone to be their leader because he knows the hard parts of Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous page, the 'garment' (שמלה) in the פסוק was read as Torah knowledge that 'covers' a person. Here the request 'be a chief over us' is explained the same way: you know the Torah matters people usually stumble on, so lead us. This prepares the next line, where the man answers honestly.

keyTerms.meaning: Grasp them, get to the bottom of them

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a discussion. The question being argued (were there trustworthy people when ירושלים was destroyed?) was raised on the previous amud.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם
phrases.english: Matters that people do not grasp
unless they first stumble in them
are in your hands;
"be a chief over us."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב קטינא's proof, which began on the previous amud as a challenge to רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That trustworthy people still existed at the time of the חורבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה ג:ו, 'שמלה לכה קצין תהיה לנו'.

steps.title: He swears that he has no Torah knowledge
steps.stepSummary: The man answers with a שבועה that he does not sit and learn and has no מקרא, משנה, or גמרא. This shows he was honest.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He will raise up on that day, saying: I will not be a binder.' The word 'raise' (ישא) means an oath, as in 'Do not raise (תשא) the name of ה׳.' 'I will not be a binder' means: I am not one of those who shut themselves into the בית המדרש. 'In my house there is no bread and no garment' means: I have no מקרא, no משנה, and no גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב קטינא's proof. The man swears the truth: he has no Torah learning, so he refuses to lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man could have accepted honor. Instead he openly admits he is not a learner. Because 'ישא' means a שבועה, the admission is backed by an oath. So רב קטינא argues there were still truthful people in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: He will raise; here it means he will swear
One who binds; here, one who shuts himself in to learn
Those who confine themselves to learning

phrases.english: "He will raise up on that day,
saying: I will not be a binder, etc." —
'raise' means nothing but an oath,
and so it says:
"Do not raise the name of the Lord" (in vain).
"I will not be a binder" —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶהְיֶה מֵחוֹבְשֵׁי עַצְמָן בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: I am not one of those who shut themselves in the study hall.
"And in my house there is no bread and no garment" —
meaning: I have in my hands no Bible,
no Mishnah, and no Gemara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the man's answer to the request in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The people of that time admitted the truth even when it hurt their honor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה ג:ז, with 'ישא' shown to mean an oath from the usage in 'לא תשא'.

steps.title: Maybe he only admitted it because he would be tested
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps he told the truth only because a lie would have been exposed right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know he was honest? Maybe that case is different: if he had told them 'I have learned,' they would have said to him, 'Tell us what you know.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof. The admission may not show honesty, because he could not have gotten away with lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being truthful only proves honesty when lying was a real option. Here, a claim to know Torah could be tested on the spot. So his admission may have been forced, not a sign of honesty.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?

phrases.english: And from where do you know?
Perhaps it is different there,
for if he had said to them 'I have learned,'
they would have said to him: 'Tell us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof built in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using this פסוק as proof of honesty, without denying the reading of the פסוק itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He had no real chance to lie, so his truthfulness proves nothing.

steps.title: He could have said he learned and forgot
steps.stepSummary: The pushback fails. He had an easy lie available, yet he swore he never learned at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could have said, 'I learned and forgot.' So what does 'I will not be a binder' mean? That he did not learn at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the pushback from step 3 and restores רב קטינא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I learned and forgot' is a lie that no test could expose. Instead, he swore he was never a learner at all. So the admission really does show honesty.

phrases.english: He could have said: 'I learned and forgot.'
What is 'I will not be a binder'? Not at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the דחיה of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a safe lie was available.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His admission was forced because he would have been tested.
steps.terutzMaskana: He chose the truth over a lie that could not be exposed, so he was honest.

steps.title: Honest about Torah, dishonest in business
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved. They were trustworthy about Torah learning but not trustworthy in business dealings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here (רב קטינא's proof) refers to Torah matters. There (רבא's statement that there were no trustworthy people) refers to business.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the conflict between רבא's statement that 'there were no אנשי אמנה' and רב קטינא's proof that people were honest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements are true, each in its own area. People told the truth about their Torah knowledge. But they could not be trusted in business, and that is the failure that led to the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; splits two sources into two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The lack of אנשי אמנה refers to dishonesty in business, not to honesty about Torah learning.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, regarding words of Torah;
there, regarding business.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב קטינא's proof stands, this resolves the original contradiction with רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two statements into two different areas of life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were honest in Torah matters and dishonest in business.

steps.title: Saving a full container of food from a fire
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows saving a whole basket of loaves, a fig cake, or a barrel of wine, even if it holds 100 meals. Others may also save food for themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may save a basket full of loaves, even if it holds 100 meals, and a round cake of dried figs, and a barrel of wine. He may say to others, 'Come and save for yourselves.' If they are clever, they settle accounts with him after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows saving large containers of food from a fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying out one whole container counts as a single act, so the size of its contents does not matter. Others who save the food may keep it as הפקר. If they are smart, they arrange to be paid for their effort after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A round cake of pressed figs

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may rescue a basket full of loaves,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֵאָה סְעוּדוֹת,
phrases.english: even though it holds a hundred meals,
and a round cake of dried figs,
and a barrel of wine.
And he may say to others:
Come and rescue for yourselves.
And if they were clever,
they settle accounts with him after Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full container of food may be saved from a fire no matter how many meals it holds.

steps.title: Where the saved items may be brought
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא allows bringing the items only to a courtyard that has an ערוב. בן בתירה allows bringing them even to one without an ערוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where may one save them? To a courtyard with an ערוב. בן בתירה says: even to one without an ערוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines where the rescued items may be carried, and records a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא permits only a place where carrying is already allowed. בן בתירה goes further and permits a courtyard with no ערוב, a more lenient position for the emergency of a fire.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard with an ערוב, where carrying is permitted

phrases.english: To where may one rescue them?
To a courtyard that has an eruv.
Ben Beteira says:
Even to one that has no eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the location rule to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת about whether the courtyard must have an ערוב.

steps.title: Wearing out clothing and utensils
steps.stepSummary: One may carry out his utensils and wear or wrap as many garments as he can. רבי יוסי limits this to 18 garments at a time, but allows repeated trips.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there he may carry out all his utensils, put on all he can wear, and wrap himself in all he can wrap. רבי יוסי says: eighteen garments. He may go back, put on more, and carry them out, and say to others, 'Come and rescue with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with saving utensils and clothing by wearing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing clothes is not normal carrying, so it is allowed. רבי יוסי caps it at 18 garments, the most a person ever normally wears. However, he lets the person go back again and again.

phrases.english: And to there he may carry out all his utensils,
and put on all that he can wear,
and wrap all that he can wrap.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר כֵּלִים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: eighteen garments.
And he may go back, put on more, and carry out,
and say to others: Come and rescue with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה from food to utensils and clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments may be worn out of a fire. רבי יוסי limits it to 18 at a time but allows repeated trips.

steps.title: But the earlier משנה allowed only three meals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The previous משנה limited saving food to three meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But the earlier clause taught three meals and no more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה by setting it against the previous משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said one may save only enough food for three meals. Our משנה allows a basket holding 100 meals. Both cannot be true as written.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But he taught in the earlier clause
three meals and no more!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first גמרא question on the new משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the earlier משנה's limit of three meals.

steps.title: רב הונא: Carrying a whole container vs. gathering loose items
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers: carrying out a full container at once is unlimited, but gathering loose food is limited to three meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is not difficult. Here, he comes to rescue. There, he comes to gather. One who comes to rescue may rescue everything. One who comes to gather may gather only food for three meals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא resolves the contradiction by splitting the two cases by what the person is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Rescuing' means taking out something already packed, like a full basket, in one go. That is allowed no matter how much it holds. 'Gathering' means collecting scattered food into a container, which is more work, so it is limited to three meals.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes to rescue: takes out a full container as is
Comes to gather: collects scattered items together

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It is not difficult;
here, where he comes to rescue;
there, where he comes to gather.
One who comes to rescue may rescue all of it.
One who comes to gather

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְקַפֵּל אֶלָּא מְזוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת.
phrases.english: may gather only food for three meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by the type of action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה deals with taking out a full container. The earlier משנה deals with gathering.

steps.title: רב: Same courtyard vs. a different courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב offers another answer. Both משניות deal with gathering. The difference is where the food is taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רב: Both deal with one who comes to gather. It is not difficult: here, to the same courtyard; there, to a different courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same contradiction, based on location rather than on the type of action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב offers a different resolution from רב הונא's: both cases involve gathering. Bringing food into the same courtyard is unlimited. Bringing it to a different courtyard is limited to three meals.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said in the name of Rav:
Both this and that refer to one who comes to gather,
and it is not difficult:
here, to the same courtyard;
there, to a different courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to רב הונא's answer in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are gathering. The same courtyard is unlimited, and a different courtyard is limited to three meals.

steps.title: Spreading out a cloak and gathering into it: which category?
steps.stepSummary: A question on רב הונא's rule. If someone spreads his טלית and keeps putting items into it, is that rescuing or gathering?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע asked: If he spread out his טלית and gathered and placed, gathered and placed, what is the law? Is it like coming to rescue, or like coming to gather?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a בעיא testing the edges of רב הונא's two categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end, everything leaves in one bundle, which looks like rescuing. But the person filled it piece by piece, which looks like gathering. The question asks which feature decides the category.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua asked:
If he spread out his cloak,
and gathered and placed, and gathered and placed,
what is the law?
Is he considered like one who comes to rescue,
or like one who comes to gather?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב הונא's distinction and tests a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether filling a spread-out טלית bit by bit counts as rescuing or as gathering.

steps.title: Proof that one large vessel counts as rescuing
steps.stepSummary: רבא said that רב חסדא was misled when he taught that a catching vessel may not hold more than three meals. This shows that filling one vessel is treated like rescuing, and it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what רבא said, we can answer the question. רבא said that רב שיזבי misled רב חסדא, and so רב חסדא taught: 'As long as he does not bring a vessel that holds more than three meals.' Since רבא called that limit a mistake, we learn that filling one vessel is like rescuing, and it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 by bringing proof from a comment of רבא. רבא called רב חסדא's three-meal limit on a vessel a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a barrel that breaks on a roof, and someone brings a vessel to catch what spills. רב חסדא limited that vessel to the size of three meals, and רבא said this limit was an error. So filling one container is not 'gathering' at all, and it has no limit. That answers our question: spreading a טלית and filling it counts as rescuing.

keyTerms.meaning: misled him; caused him to make an error
it is treated like one who comes to rescue

phrases.english: From that which Rava said:
Rav Sheizvi misled Rav Chisda,
and he taught: provided that one does not bring a vessel
phrases.notes: This is about a barrel that broke on a roof on שבת.

phrases.english: that holds more than three meals,
conclude from this: it is like one who comes to rescue,
and it is perfectly fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: Whether filling one spread-out container, such as a טלית, counts as rescuing (no limit) or as gathering (limited)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement that רב חסדא's three-meal limit on a catching vessel was a mistake

steps.title: What exactly was the mistake?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא what was wrong with רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: What was the mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא how he knows that רב חסדא's limit was wrong. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's limit sounds reasonable, because the earlier משנה also limited food to three meals. So רב נחמן בר יצחק wants to know the source that shows the limit was an error.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
What is the mistake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רבא's claim in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא's three-meal limit on the vessel counts as a mistake

steps.title: The ברייתא bans only a second vessel, not a big one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only forbids bringing ANOTHER vessel to catch or to attach. In the same single vessel, one may save as much as he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It is taught, 'As long as he does not bring another vessel to catch, or another vessel to attach.' So it is only another vessel that is forbidden. In that same vessel, he may save as much as he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the error. The ברייתא only limits bringing extra vessels, not the size of the one vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא read a size limit into the ruling, but the source never mentions size. The only restriction is adding a second vessel. So one vessel of any size counts as rescuing.

keyTerms.meaning: and attach (it next to the roof)

steps.whatToRemember: Saving into one vessel or container, even a large one or a spread-out טלית, is 'rescuing' and has no limit. The three-meal limit applies only to gathering loose food piece by piece.

phrases.english: He said to him: for it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא כְּלִי אַחֵר וְיִקְלוֹט,
phrases.english: Provided that he does not bring another vessel and catch,
or another vessel and attach.
It is another vessel that is not allowed,
but in that same vessel —
he may rescue as much as he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא restricts only a second vessel. There is no size limit on the one vessel.

steps.title: Why pay helpers for ownerless food?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says clever helpers 'make a calculation' with the owner after שבת. But food rescued on שבת is הפקר, so what is there to calculate?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And a round cake of dried figs, etc.' What is this 'calculation' for? Aren't the helpers acquiring the food from ownerless property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and challenges it. Why would helpers settle accounts with the owner, if what they rescued already belongs to them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner told others, 'Come and rescue for yourselves,' so whatever they save becomes theirs as הפקר. They owe him nothing, so any 'calculation' seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: a round cake of pressed dried figs

phrases.english: And a round cake of dried figs, etc.
What is the calculation doing here?
Aren't they acquiring from ownerless property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line about making a calculation with the owner after שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rescued food is הפקר and belongs to the helpers, so no calculation should be needed.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is extra piety
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה is describing מדת חסידות. Pious helpers choose to return the food and take payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The משנה here is teaching a standard of piety.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the calculation is not required by law. It describes pious people going beyond the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legally the helpers keep what they saved. Pious helpers return it to the owner anyway and take only payment for their work.

keyTerms.meaning: a standard of piety beyond the letter of the law

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They taught a standard of piety here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as voluntary piety
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The calculation seemed pointless, because the food is הפקר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pious helpers give the food back by choice and are paid for their effort.

steps.title: רבא: pious people don't take שבת wages
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects this: truly pious people would never accept payment for work done on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do pious people take payment for שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking שכר שבת is something a real חסיד would avoid. So the people in the משנה cannot be the pious people רב חסדא described.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Do pious people take payment for Shabbat?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's whole explanation that the helpers are חסידים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Pious people would not accept שכר שבת, yet the משנה has them take payment.

steps.title: רבא: a God-fearing person who is not a full חסיד
steps.stepSummary: The helper is a ירא שמים. He does not want to benefit from another person's property, but he also does not want to work for nothing. Clever helpers know this payment is not שכר שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Here we are dealing with a God-fearing person. He is not comfortable benefiting from others, and he is also not comfortable working for free. This is what the משנה means: if they are clever, and know that in a case like this it is not 'payment for שבת', they make a calculation with him after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own explanation. The helpers are God-fearing middle-ground people, and the clever ones know they may settle up after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a person gives the food back so he will not profit from someone else's loss. He takes a small payment so his work is not for nothing. The 'clever' ones understand that in this situation the payment does not count as forbidden שכר שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: he is not comfortable with it
wages for work done on שבת (normally forbidden)

steps.confusionAlert: 'פיקחין' here does not mean the helpers are clever at getting more money. It means they know the הלכה: in this case the payment is not forbidden שכר שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Here we are dealing with a God-fearing person,
and he is not comfortable benefiting from others,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחִנָּם נָמֵי לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִיטְרַח.
phrases.english: and he is also not comfortable exerting himself for free.
And this is what it is saying:
And if they are clever,

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָדְעִי דִּכְהַאי גַּוְונָא לָאו שְׂכַר שַׁבָּת הוּא,
phrases.english: knowing that in such a case it is not Shabbat wages,
they make a calculation with him after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא בִּירֵא שָׁמַיִם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining who the helpers are and reinterpreting 'פיקחין'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either no calculation makes sense, or the helpers are חסידים.
steps.terutzMaskana: God-fearing helpers who know the הלכה return the food and settle up after שבת. In this case that is not forbidden שכר שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'calculation' in the משנה is about a God-fearing helper who returns the rescued food but takes payment for his effort. This is allowed because here it is not considered שכר שבת.

steps.title: Why 'for yourselves' for food but 'with me' for clothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה tells others to rescue 'לכם' when talking about food, but 'עמי' when talking about clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And to where may one rescue, etc.' Why is it different here, where it says 'for yourselves,' and why is it different there, where it says 'with me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a difference in wording between two parts of the משנה and asks for the reason. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With food, the owner says, 'Come and rescue for yourselves.' With clothing, he says, 'Come and rescue with me.' The גמרא wants to know why the wording changes.

phrases.english: And to where may one rescue, etc.
What is different here, that it teaches 'for yourselves',
and what is different here, that it teaches 'with me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new clarification about the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the food case says 'לכם' while the clothing case says 'עמי'

steps.title: Food is limited, clothing is not
steps.stepSummary: With food, only three meals are of use to the owner on שבת, so the rest is 'for yourselves.' Clothing is useful to him all day, so others save 'with me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: With food it says 'for yourselves,' because only food for three meals is useful to him. But with clothing it says 'with me,' because it is useful to him all day long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the different wording matches the different limits on food and on clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the owner can only use three meals' worth of food, so anything beyond that is of use only to the others, and it is 'theirs.' Clothing stays useful to him all day, because he can wear and change into those garments throughout the day. So the helpers are saving for him, together 'with' him.

phrases.english: They said:
Regarding food, it teaches 'for yourselves' —

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא קָא חֲזֵי אֶלָּא מְזוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת.
phrases.english: because only food for three meals is fit for him.
But regarding garments, it teaches 'with me' —
because it is fit for him the whole day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only three meals of food are of use to the owner on שבת, so extra food is 'לכם.' Clothing is useful to him all day, so it is 'עמי.'

steps.title: רבי מאיר: wear, carry out, remove, all day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: one may wear garments, go out, take them off, and repeat this all day long. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: He wears, carries out, and takes off. Then he goes back, wears, carries out, and takes off, even all day long. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about rescuing clothing by wearing it out of the fire. This step gives רבי מאיר's view: there is no limit on how many trips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going out wearing clothes is not an act of carrying at all, since one wears them in the normal way, so it is allowed. רבי מאיר lets a person repeat the trips as many times as he wants. This fits the 'all day' idea from the previous step.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
He wears, carries out, and takes off,
and goes back and wears, carries out, and takes off,
and even the entire day —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's rule about clothing (step 8).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one may wear garments out of a fire and repeat the trip with no limit, all day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: eighteen garments, listed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says one may wear only eighteen garments, and the ברייתא lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Eighteen garments. These are the eighteen garments: a cloak, a cape, a hollow belt, a wide linen garment, a shirt, an outer robe, a head kerchief, two straps, two shoes, two socks, two boots, a belt on his waist, a hat on his head, and a scarf on his neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's opposing view and lists exactly which eighteen garments one may wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי limits the rescue to eighteen garments, which is the full outfit a person normally wears. The list counts single items and pairs (two straps, two shoes, two socks, two boots) to reach eighteen.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: wear garments out with no limit, all day. רבי יוסי: only eighteen garments, the normal full outfit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר כֵּלִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: eighteen garments,
and these are the eighteen garments:
a cloak, a cape, and a hollow belt,
a wide linen garment, and a shirt,
and an outer robe, and a kerchief,
and two straps, and two shoes,
and two socks, and two boots,
and a belt on his waist, and a hat on his head,
and a scarf on his neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, one may wear out only eighteen specific garments.

steps.title: Spreading a goat hide over burning furniture
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן ננס rules that one may spread a goat hide over a box, chest, or closet that caught fire, because the fire only singes the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון בן ננס says: You may spread a goat's hide over a box, a chest, or a closet that caught fire, because the fire only singes the hide.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי שמעון בן ננס allows covering burning wooden furniture with a moist goat hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hide is moist, so the fire only scorches it and does not burn it. You are not pouring water or directly putting out the fire. You are simply placing a protective cover, and the fire stops on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A box, a chest, and a closet (wooden furniture)
Singes or scorches (does not truly burn)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the whole משנה: protecting property by blocking the fire, without directly putting it out.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas says:
One may spread out a goat's hide
over a box, a chest, or a closet
that caught fire,
phrases.notes: Literally: that the fire took hold of them.

phrases.english: because it only singes.
phrases.notes: The fire scorches the moist hide but cannot burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. The earlier discussion was about rescuing items from a fire. Now the topic is stopping the fire from spreading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may cover burning furniture with a moist goat hide, since it only singes and is not a direct act of extinguishing.

steps.title: Building a barrier of vessels to stop the fire
steps.stepSummary: One may build a barrier out of any vessels, full or empty, so the fire does not spread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you may make a barrier out of all kinds of vessels, both full and empty, so that the fire will not pass.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows lining up vessels as a wall so the fire cannot spread further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Full' here includes vessels full of water. If the fire reaches them and they burst, the water puts the fire out. That is only an indirect result (גרם כיבוי), and the תנא קמא permits it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Full' does not just mean full of anything. The point is that even vessels full of water are allowed. That is exactly what רבי יוסי argues about next.

phrases.english: And one may make a barrier with all vessels,
both full and empty,
so that the fire will not pass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second permitted way to protect property from the fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrier of vessels, even vessels full of water, is permitted. Causing the fire to go out indirectly is allowed according to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids new clay vessels full of water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי forbids using new earthenware vessels full of water, because they will crack in the heat and put out the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי forbids using new clay vessels full of water, because they cannot withstand the fire. They will crack open and put out the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the previous ruling for one specific case: new clay pots filled with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New clay pots are certain to burst from the heat, which makes the extinguishing very likely. רבי יוסי forbids even causing the fire to go out this way (גרם כיבוי). The תנא קמא permits it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic מחלוקת about גרם כיבוי (indirectly causing a fire to go out). The rest of the סוגיא builds on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei forbids
new earthenware vessels full of water,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְקַבֵּל אֶת הָאוּר
phrases.english: because they cannot withstand the fire
and they burst and extinguish the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס חֲדָשִׁים מְלֵאִין מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the previous step for one specific kind of full vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי when the vessels will surely burst and put out the fire.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא allows causing a fire to go out indirectly (גרם כיבוי). רבי יוסי forbids it when the extinguishing is certain.

steps.title: רב: water may be placed on the unburnt side of a burning garment
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: if a garment caught fire on one side, you may put water on the other side, and if the fire goes out, so be it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If a garment caught fire on one side, you may put water on its other side. If the fire then goes out, it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling from רב. You may wet the part of a garment that is not yet burning, so that the fire stops when it reaches that part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the water is not poured on the fire itself. It is placed ahead of the fire, so the fire goes out only indirectly. רב permits this kind of גרם כיבוי, in line with the תנא קמא of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
If it goes out, it goes out (that is acceptable)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: טַלִּית שֶׁאָחַז בָּהּ הָאוּר מִצַּד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: A garment that caught fire on one side —
one may place water on it on the other side,
and if it is extinguished, it is extinguished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's idea of indirect extinguishing to the case of a burning garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may deliberately place water on the unburnt side of a garment, even though this will cause the fire to go out indirectly.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows only wearing the garment or reading the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא. It says you may wear a burning garment or read a burning ספר תורה, and if the fire goes out, it goes out. It does not mention placing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: A garment that caught fire on one side, you may spread it out and cover yourself with it, and if the fire goes out, it goes out. Likewise, a ספר תורה that caught fire, you may open it and read from it, and if the fire goes out, it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב. The ברייתא allows only normal, permitted actions that happen to put out the fire, not deliberately placing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the person is simply wearing or reading, and the fire may go out by itself. Since it does not allow placing water, it seems that deliberately setting water near the fire is forbidden. The answer to this challenge comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He spreads it out (to wear it)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say placing water is forbidden. The גמרא is reading that from what the ברייתא leaves out: it lists only a normal, permitted action and not water.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: טַלִּית שֶׁאָחַז בָּהּ הָאוּר מִצַּד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: A garment that caught fire on one side —
one may spread it out and cover himself with it,
and if it is extinguished, it is extinguished.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁאָחַז בּוֹ הָאוּר —
phrases.english: And likewise, a Torah scroll that caught fire —
one may open it and read from it,
and if it is extinguished, it is extinguished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's ruling in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may place water on the unburnt side of a garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows only a normal, permitted act (wearing or reading) that happens to put out the fire. This implies that deliberately placing water, which is what רב permits, is forbidden.
